units.translation: c. τῖφος: the marshy place where the boar spent its time. About the boar, Herodorus (31 FGrH 24 J.) also says that he carried it to the gates of Mycenae and set it down. "ἰλλόμενον" means "bound." Through the word "ἀπεθήκατο" the strength of the one carrying it is shown, that he did so easily.

131. σὺν καί οἱ Ὕλας: This man was Heracles' beloved, son of Theiodamas son of Dryops. So Mnaseas (fr. 10 M. III 151). Hellanicus (4 FGrH 131a J.) names Theiomene instead of Theiodamas.

b. φύλακος: in Ionic fashion for "the guard." For the Ionians make genitives into nominatives: "of the guard" becomes "the guard," "of the witness" becomes "the witness." The first syllable of φύλακος should be accented acute; but Herodian (I 150, 3 L.) accents the last syllable. φορεύς means "the one who carries." Lm(P)

24 Ναύπλιολ — ἐστίν in L : ὁ Ν. οὗτος ἀπὸ τοῦ παλαιοῦ... in P
This man is descended from the ancient Nauplius. He speaks of Proetus, the enemy of Bellerophon and husband of Anteia; Homer (Iliad Z 152 ff.) also knows this.

139-44a. Ἴδμων δ’ ὑστάτ〈ιος〉: Chamaeleon (fr. 6 Koepke) says that Thestor was called Idmon among the ancients because of his experience; others say that Thestor also sailed with the Argonauts. Deiiochus (fr. 1 M. II 17) says that Amphiaraus sailed with them. Idmon, as Pherecydes (3 FGrH 108 J.) relates, was the child of Asteria, daughter of Coronus, and Apollo; from him and Laothoe came Thestor; and from Thestor, Calchas. Idmon was killed in Mariandynia by a boar. That Idmon was the son of Abas, Herodorus (31 FGrH 44 J.) also says.
